label: copy-phase input e (the original 3rd token fed back), esp. when the next output is e/y
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.007% of steps) that fires only in the copy phase and only when the fed-back input token is e (100% of activations; never in the original or delimiter phases, never on any other input token). Every activation is a repeat occurrence of e, and it is concentrated at recall_idx 3 (78% of mass, i.e. e was original token 2), with recall 2-4 covering 98%. Long sequences (L=8-9) dominate. Magnitude is highest when the token being output is e or y (e.g. original prefix ..e e.. or ..e y r..), and next_out r is enriched. Copy-phase e alone has recall 1.0 but precision 0.005: most copy-phase e inputs do not activate it, and the gating context is only partly captured by position, length and the e/y output condition. Tighter conditions (recall_idx 3, L>=8) raise precision to ~0.41 but lose recall.
